HOUSEHOLD CONTENTS INSURANCE
GENERAL POLICY CONDITIONS - PROPERTY DAMAGE COVER
Policy wording "WD-2026" - Mobility Equipment and Recovery Edition

These conditions apply together with the General Contract Provisions and with the
Schedule, both of which form part of this contract. Sums insured, limits,
deductibles, periods and percentages shown in square brackets are those stated in
the Schedule.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 1 - PURPOSE AND KEY CONCEPTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 What this insurance does

This insurance protects the policyholder against the financial consequences of
the loss of, or physical damage to, insured movable property. The perils that can
be insured are the ones bundled together in these conditions - among them theft
and the damage done in the course of it, break-in damage, fire, escape of water
and the natural hazards. Which of the insurable perils are actually covered is
agreed between insurer and policyholder and recorded in the schedule.

Where insured property is taken, destroyed or damaged, the insurer indemnifies
the value of that property, or the cost of putting it back, on the basis set out
in Part 6 and within the sums insured and sub-limits agreed. Where property that
was taken is found again, the insurer also carries the cost of getting it back
and of making it usable, within the heads listed in Part 5.

Two lines run through the whole of this wording. The first divides making good
the damage an insured event caused from keeping property in order generally: the
first is indemnified, the second is not, whoever performs it and however it is
described. The second divides the item the event reached from everything else in
the household: the first is made good, the second is not, however sensible it may
be to attend to it at the same time.

1.2 How the wording is to be read

Personal designations are to be understood as gender-neutral throughout; no
parallel male and female forms are used.

1.3 Explanation of recurring terms (not legally binding)

Policyholder - the insurer's contracting party and the purchaser of the cover.

Insured event - the event for which the insurer pays.

Exclusion - a peril, a type of damage or an item of property for which no cover
exists. Exclusions delimit what has been promised and keep the cover calculable.

Affected item - an item of insured property which was taken, destroyed, damaged
or lost in the insured event, and which is identified as such in the itemisation
under 7.1.10. An item that was not taken and on which no damage from the event is
established is not an affected item, whatever its place in the same household and
whatever its relation to the affected one.

Recovery - the process of getting an item that was taken back into the
policyholder's possession from the place where it is found.

Repair cost - the outlay directed at making good the physical damage caused by
the insured event on an affected item. Outlay that pursues any other purpose is
not a repair cost, however it may be described or invoiced.

Ancillary charge - any charge raised alongside the itemised labour and materials:
call-out and travel, carriage and dispatch, assembly and fitting, small parts and
sundries, administration, handling and comparable items. An ancillary charge
shares the fate of the work it accompanies.

Sub-limit - a monetary ceiling that applies within the sum insured to a defined
class of property or to a defined head of cost. Where a sub-limit applies, the
class or head is indemnified only up to that ceiling; the excess is borne by the
policyholder. Where the loss on that class or head remains below the ceiling, the
sub-limit does not reduce the indemnity.

Duties - the things the policyholder must do or refrain from doing before, during
and after an insured event.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 2 - INSURED PERILS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 The perils that can be covered

The insurer indemnifies insured property that is taken, destroyed or damaged by,
or lost as a consequence of, the following events:

  (a) THEFT of insured property, and the damage done to insured property in the
      course of a theft or an attempted theft;

  (b) BREAK-IN DAMAGE to the insured premises or to a locked receptacle or
      fastening;

  (c) FIRE GROUP - fire; lightning strike; overvoltage caused by lightning;
      explosion; deflagration; implosion; impact or crash of an aircraft, its
      parts or its cargo; impact of a vehicle; scorching; smoke and soot;

  (d) ESCAPE OF WATER;

  (e) NATURAL HAZARDS, in two tiers:
        (e1) storm and hail;
        (e2) the further natural hazards - flood, backing-up of water,
             earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load, avalanche and
             volcanic eruption.

2.2 How the groups combine

Each of the groups (a), (b), (c), (d) and (e1) can be taken separately. The
further natural hazards under (e2) can only be taken in combination with one or
more of the other groups.

2.3 Theft and the damage done in the course of it

2.3.1 What the peril is
Theft is the taking of insured property from the policyholder's possession
against the policyholder's will and with the intention of keeping it. Covered
under this heading are:
  (a) the loss of the item taken, where it is not recovered;
  (b) the physical damage done to the item in the course of the theft or the
      attempted theft, including the damage done in overcoming, forcing, cutting
      or breaking the fastening, mounting or securing device holding it, and the
      damage found on it when it is recovered;
  (c) the physical damage done in the course of the same event to the fabric,
      fittings, fastenings and locking equipment of the insured premises or of
      the place where the item was secured.

2.3.2 Recovery of an item that was taken
Where an item that was taken is found again, the policyholder notifies the
insurer without delay. Getting it back is treated as a mitigation of the loss:
the costs of the recovery are indemnified under 5.2.2, and the damage found on
the item is made good under 7.1.

Where the item is recovered before the indemnity for its loss is paid, it is
treated as a damaged item and 7.1.1(b) applies. Where it is recovered after that
indemnity is paid, the policyholder either surrenders it to the insurer or
retains it against repayment.

2.3.3 Damage excluded within this peril
Not covered:
  (a) property mislaid, misplaced, forgotten or left behind, and a shortfall
      established only on a later review and not attributable to an identified
      event;
  (b) property surrendered voluntarily, including on a deception or a false
      pretext;
  (c) damage attributable to use, wear, ageing, corrosion, a pre-existing defect
      or the want of servicing, as distinct from damage done in the course of the
      event (3.1.6);
  (d) an item on which no damage from the event is established, and an item that
      was not taken.

Where an item that was taken is recovered in undamaged condition, the loss under
2.3.1(a) ceases with the recovery and no indemnity arises under 7.1.1(b) in
respect of that item. The recovery costs under 5.2.2 remain payable. Renewing,
exchanging or upgrading an assembly of such an item afterwards is an election of
the policyholder and is governed by 3.1.6 and 7.1.8(c).

2.4 Break-in damage

Break-in damage is the physical damage caused where a person breaks into, forces
open, breaks out of, or attempts by comparable means to enter the insured
premises, a part of them, or a locked receptacle or fastening, whether or not
anything is taken.

2.5 Fire group, escape of water and natural hazards

2.5.1 The fire group covers fire - a combustion that has started without a hearth
intended for it, or that has escaped such a hearth, and that is capable of
spreading under its own power - together with lightning strike, overvoltage
caused by lightning, explosion, deflagration, implosion, aircraft impact, vehicle
impact, scorching, and smoke and soot. Damage from the gradual action of smoke or
soot is not covered.

2.5.2 Escaping water means water that has emerged contrary to its intended
purpose from the water, heating, air-conditioning, extinguishing or comparable
installations of the building in which the insured property is located.

2.5.3 Storm means a weather-driven movement of air reaching at least the gale
threshold on the recognised scale of wind strength; hail means solid
precipitation in the form of grains of ice. The further natural hazards are
flood, backing-up of water, earthquake, ground subsidence, landslip, snow load,
avalanche and volcanic eruption, each as customarily defined.

2.5.4 Not covered within these groups is damage caused by storm surge; by the
penetration of precipitation or dirt through openings that were not properly
closed; by groundwater save where it emerged at the surface as a result of
precipitation or overflow; by earthquake within the fire group; and by drought or
desiccation.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 3 - EXCLUSIONS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 General exclusions

3.1.1 War
Damage caused by war, warlike events, civil war, revolution, rebellion or
insurrection is not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.2 Civil commotion
Damage caused by internal civil unrest is not covered, irrespective of any
contributing causes.

3.1.3 Nuclear energy
Damage caused by nuclear energy, nuclear radiation or radioactive substances is
not covered, irrespective of any contributing causes.

3.1.4 Liability risks
Claims of third parties against the policyholder, and any outlay directed at
covering, assessing, administering or settling such claims, are not the subject
of this contract.

3.1.5 Administration and claim handling
Outlay arising from a service, assistance, representation, handling or comparable
arrangement, and any charge for opening, administering, processing or presenting
a claim file, is not indemnifiable. This applies irrespective of whether the
charge is raised by a party that also renders an indemnifiable benefit, and
irrespective of the stage of the claim at which it arises. Charges payable to a
third party as a condition of obtaining the release of a recovered item are not
charges of this kind and fall under 5.2.2.

3.1.6 Servicing, upkeep and improvement
Outlay directed at the servicing, maintenance, tuning, adjustment, overhaul,
cleaning, inspection, general condition or improvement of property is not
indemnifiable, however closely it follows an insured event in time, whoever
performs it, and whether it is described as a service, an overhaul, a tune-up, a
check or a refurbishment. Bringing an item back to the condition it was in
immediately before the event is making good; bringing it to a better or merely a
tidier condition is not.

The renewal or exchange of a part is not made indemnifiable by the part being one
that an insured event could have damaged. Where a part is renewed in the course
of, on the occasion of, or as an element of a service, an overhaul or a general
check, it is renewed for its own condition and not to make good the event, and it
falls under this clause whatever the part and however the line is worded.
Likewise, where the policyholder elects to renew or upgrade an assembly that
carries no damage from the event, the outlay falls under this clause and under
7.1.8(c) in its entirety, and not merely as to the difference in grade.

Where an invoice is directed predominantly at work of this kind, the labour of
every grade, the sundries, the assembly, the carriage and the attendance charges
on it share that character and are not indemnifiable either (7.1.10).

3.1.7 Additional, supplementary and unaffected property
The supply of property that adds to, supplements, protects, secures, equips or
accompanies an affected item, without itself having been affected by the insured
event, is not indemnifiable. Nor is any measure directed at a further item of the
household that the event did not reach.

3.2 Exclusions within the theft peril

See 2.3.3.

3.3 Exclusions within the remaining perils

See 2.5.4.

3.4 Outlay that is not a repair or recovery cost

Outlay that does not represent the value of an affected item, the cost of making
good the damage to it, or a head expressly listed in Part 5, is not indemnified.
The delimitation is governed by 7.1.5 to 7.1.10.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 4 - INSURED PROPERTY, INSURED LOCATION, DEDUCTIBLES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 What is insured

Insured property comprises the movable items belonging to the household of the
policyholder and serving its private use, insofar as the policyholder owns them
or bears the risk for them, together with the classes of property described in
4.2 within the sub-limits stated in the schedule.

4.2 The categories defined

4.2.1 General household effects
Movable items of ordinary household use. This class carries no sub-limit of its
own; it is indemnified up to the sum insured stated in the schedule.

4.2.2 Mobility equipment
Cycles and comparable means of personal transport propelled by muscle power or
electrically assisted, together with the frames, wheels, drives, transmission,
braking, steering and control assemblies, batteries and permanently fitted parts
belonging to them, form a single class of property. Indemnity for this class is
subject to the mobility equipment sub-limit stated in the schedule, applied in
the aggregate per insured event across all affected items of the class, all
trades and all invoices, and covering the value of the items, the making good of
the damage done to them and the recovery costs under 5.2.2 together.

Where the aggregate indemnifiable loss on this class exceeds the sub-limit, the
indemnity is confined to the sub-limit and is applied rateably to the
indemnifiable lines concerned; the balance is borne by the policyholder. Where it
does not exceed the sub-limit, the indemnifiable loss is paid in full.

4.2.3 Accessories, protective and supplementary equipment
Detachable accessories, carriers, covers, lighting sets, protective and safety
equipment worn by the user, locks and fastenings, tracking, marking and
monitoring devices and comparable supplementary items are insured only where they
are themselves affected items. They are not indemnified where they are procured,
renewed, added or supplemented in connection with the loss or with the
replacement of an affected item without having been themselves taken or damaged,
whatever their functional or practical value to the user (3.1.7).

4.2.4 Valuables and means of payment
Items of concentrated value and the means of payment form separate classes, each
subject to the sub-limit stated in the schedule for it.

4.3 Property not insured

Not insured:
  (a) property used predominantly for a trade, business or profession;
  (b) motor vehicles requiring registration, watercraft and aircraft, and their
      parts and accessories;
  (c) electronically stored data and programs, and the restoration, migration or
      re-registration of software, media content, user accounts and comparable
      intangible items;
  (d) documents, entitlements and credit balances as such;
  (e) property acquired on the occasion of the loss which does not replace an
      affected item of the same kind and intended purpose (3.1.7).

4.4 Optionally insurable

Individual items may be scheduled at an agreed value, and classes of property may
be insured at raised sub-limits, where this is agreed and recorded in the
schedule.

4.5 The insured location

The insured location is the dwelling stated in the schedule together with the
ancillary rooms and stores belonging to it. Insured mobility equipment is
additionally covered while in use, in transit or secured away from the insured
location, insofar as this is agreed in the schedule and subject to 9.1.3.

4.6 Several persons entitled

Where several persons are entitled under this contract, the insurer may render
its benefit to any one of them with effect for all.

4.7 Deductibles

A deductible is the share of the indemnity, or the amount, that the policyholder
bears itself per insured event. Deductibles can be agreed individually and may
differ from one insured peril and one insured benefit to another. Each is set out
in the schedule. The deductible is applied once per insured event to the covered
settlement, irrespective of the number of items, trades or invoices involved.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 5 - INSURED COSTS
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 Which costs are covered

The insurer reimburses the following costs where they were necessary as a
consequence of an insured event and were actually incurred:
  (a) the cost of averting or mitigating the loss;
  (b) the cost of recovering an item that was taken;
  (c) the cost of making the insured premises or the place of securing safe and
      closed again after a break-in;
  (d) the cost of moving and protecting insured property;
  (e) the cost of disposing of destroyed insured property.

Reimbursement of each of these heads is limited to the amount agreed for it. This
list is exhaustive. A head of cost that does not fall within it, and that is not a
repair cost within the meaning of 7.1.7, is not insured.

5.2 The cost heads defined

5.2.1 Averting and mitigating the loss
Costs of measures taken during or immediately after the insured event to prevent
the loss from occurring or from increasing, capped at [amount] per insured event.

5.2.2 Recovering an item that was taken
Where an item that was taken is found again, the insurer reimburses what has to
be spent to get it back into the policyholder's possession and into a state in
which it can be moved:
  (a) the attendance of a trade at the place where the item is found, and the
      further attendances actually required by the recovery, each such attendance
      being reimbursable in its own right by way of departure from 7.1.8(f);
  (b) the opening, cutting, drilling, releasing or removal of a lock, fastening,
      chain, mounting or securing device holding the item, whether that device
      belongs to the policyholder or to another, together with the labour of every
      grade employed on that work and the sundry materials consumed by it;
  (c) charges that a third party holding the item requires as a condition of its
      release - storage, custody, handling, impound and comparable charges -
      insofar as the policyholder cannot avoid them;
  (d) the transport of the recovered item from the place where it is found to the
      insured location or to the place of repair.

Indemnity under this head is capped at [amount] per insured event and, for an item
of the class under 4.2.2, is additionally subject to the sub-limit for that class.

5.2.3 Securing the premises again
Costs of closing, securing and making safe the insured premises or the place of
securing after a break-in, including the provisional and the permanent renewal of
the affected locking and fastening equipment.

5.2.4 Moving and protecting property
Costs incurred in moving, altering or protecting property, where those measures
serve to secure or reinstate insured property.

5.2.5 Disposal
Costs of removing and disposing of destroyed insured property and of the parts
taken out in the course of the covered repair, reimbursed once per insured event
for the material concerned.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 6 - BASIS OF COVER AND PREMIUM
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 Insurable value

The insurable value forms the basis for calculating the indemnity. It is
determined separately for each class of property under 4.2.

6.2 Replacement value

6.2.1 What is insured is the amount that would have to be spent to procure
property of the same kind and quality in new condition at the time of the insured
event.

6.2.2 For items whose current value has fallen to a substantial extent below the
replacement value - in particular through age, wear or technical obsolescence -
the current value applies in place of the replacement value.

6.2.3 Where an affected item is repaired rather than replaced, the insurable
value is not the measure of the indemnity; the necessary repair costs under
7.1.1(b) are, up to that value.

6.3 Relationship between basis of cover and sub-limits

The basis of cover under 6.2 does not displace a sub-limit. Where a class of
property carries a sub-limit, the sub-limit determines the ceiling of the
indemnity for that class even where the insurable value and the repair and
recovery costs together demonstrably exceed it. Conversely, a sub-limit is a
ceiling and not a fixed benefit: where the indemnifiable loss on that class is
lower, the indemnity is the loss, and where the class carries no sub-limit the
indemnifiable loss is paid within the sum insured.

6.4 Permanently devalued property

For property that can no longer be used for its purpose, only the achievable sale
price is insured.

6.5 How the premium is calculated

The bases for calculating the premium are the sum insured, the sub-limits agreed,
the deductible agreed, the security arrangements agreed, other agreed features
material to the premium calculation, and the adjustment factor.

6.6 Adjustment of cover and premium

Where cover is adjusted, the premium changes accordingly. The adjustment factor
changes with effect from 1 January of each year in line with the movement of the
relevant published price indices, weighted as agreed and rounded to two decimal
places.

6.7 Subsequent change in a premium-rating feature

Where a rating circumstance subsequently changes and a higher premium results,
the insurer may demand the higher premium from the point at which the change is
notified. Where such a circumstance ceases to apply and a lower premium results,
the insurer must reduce the premium from the point at which it becomes aware of
that.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 7 - CALCULATION AND PAYMENT OF THE INDEMNITY
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 Basis of calculation

7.1.1 The insurer reimburses:
  (a) for taken, destroyed or lost items that are not recovered - the insurable
      value under Part 6 at the time of the insured event;
  (b) for damaged items, and for recovered items on which damage is found - the
      necessary repair costs at the time of the insured event, together with any
      diminution in value the repair does not offset, capped at the insurable
      value of the item;
  (c) for the fabric, fittings and locking equipment of the insured premises or of
      the place of securing - the necessary repair costs.

Where the property concerned belongs to a class carrying a sub-limit, the
indemnity under (a), (b) or (c) is in every case confined to that sub-limit.

7.1.2 Price increases occurring between the insured event and the replacement are
indemnified where the replacement is secured within [number] months.

7.1.3 The achievable sale price of remains and of unusable parts taken out is set
off in calculating the indemnity.

7.1.4 Where an item is recovered, 2.3.2 applies.

7.1.5 Extent of the indemnity
Indemnity is confined to the affected items. Work carried out on, and property
supplied for, an item that was not itself affected is not covered, even where it
is carried out so that the affected and unaffected items correspond in condition
or equipment; for reasons of convenience or economy; as a precaution against a
future event; at the same time as covered work or in the course of it; or by the
same trade as the covered work and invoiced together with it.

7.1.6 Sets and matched items
Where one item of a set, suite or pair was affected, indemnity is confined to
that item and does not extend to the remaining, unaffected items, whatever the
loss of uniformity or completeness.

7.1.7 What the repair and recovery cost comprises
The necessary repair costs under 7.1.1(b) include, insofar as they are directed
at an affected item:
  (a) the removal, dismantling and disposal of the damaged assemblies and parts;
  (b) replacement assemblies, components and parts of a type, quality, grade and
      specification corresponding to those fitted immediately before the insured
      event;
  (c) the assembly, fitting, mounting, adjustment, alignment and functional
      testing of those replacement parts on the item, this being part of the
      repair and not a separate supply service;
  (d) the labour hours needed for that work, at every grade of personnel employed
      on it - skilled, qualified, assisting, apprenticed and trainee alike - at
      the rates customary in the trade concerned, with the hours of each grade
      stated separately;
  (e) the small parts, fixings, lubricants, sealing and comparable sundry
      materials consumed by the work, whether itemised individually or collected
      under a single sundry heading;
  (f) the carriage, dispatch, delivery and freight of the replacement parts to
      the place of repair and of the affected item to and from that place, this
      being a necessary element of restoring the item rather than an accommodation
      to the policyholder;
  (g) the attendance of the trade at the insured location or at the place of
      repair or recovery;
  (h) the cleaning of the item where the event made it necessary.

The recovery costs under 5.2.2 are additional to these and are governed by that
clause.

7.1.8 Outlay that is not a repair or recovery cost
The following are not indemnified, however they may be described, bundled or
invoiced, by whichever trade they are raised, and irrespective of whether they
appear on an invoice that also contains covered work:

  (a) measures directed at the servicing, maintenance, tuning, adjustment,
      overhaul, cleaning, inspection, general condition, upkeep or improvement of
      property (3.1.6), together with the labour of every grade, the sundries, the
      assembly, the carriage and the attendance charges belonging to them;

  (b) the supply of property that adds to, supplements, protects, secures, equips
      or accompanies an affected item without itself having been affected, and
      every measure directed at a further item of the household that the event did
      not reach (3.1.7, 7.1.5), together with the ancillary charges belonging to
      them;

  (c) the improvement element where a replacement of a higher grade, superior
      material, greater capability or premium range is chosen; indemnity is
      limited to the cost of the standard-grade equivalent corresponding to what
      was fitted before the loss (7.1.9). Where the assembly being replaced
      carries no damage from the insured event, so that the outlay is an election
      of the policyholder rather than the making good of a loss, no part of it is
      indemnified, and the standard-grade limitation does not operate to bring a
      residue of it into the cover;

  (d) outlay belonging to a trade's own business operation rather than to the
      indemnifiable work - its own tools and consumable small equipment as such,
      its own diagnostic and measuring devices, provisioning and catering for its
      own personnel, and general administrative, handling, order-processing,
      claim-processing, file-opening or documentation charges levied in addition
      to the itemised labour and materials (3.1.5);

  (e) charges of the kind described in 3.1.4 and 3.1.5;

  (f) attendance charges on an invoice on which nothing is indemnifiable; and
      attendances beyond those required by the covered work. Where an attendance
      was actually required by the covered repair or by the recovery under 5.2.2,
      it is reimbursed, and a further such attendance is not treated as a
      duplicate merely because an earlier one was already charged;

  (g) the same item of cost where it is invoiced more than once in respect of the
      same insured event, whether by one trade or across several; only the first
      such charge is indemnified.

7.1.9 No improvement on the pre-loss standard
The indemnity proceeds on the basis of the type, quality, grade, capability and
specification of the affected item and its parts immediately before the insured
event. Where a higher specification is chosen instead, the difference is borne by
the policyholder. Where the part fitted before the loss is no longer obtainable,
the nearest currently available equivalent of the same grade sets the ceiling; an
unavoidable difference is not treated as an improvement, a chosen one is.

7.1.10 Itemisation, evidence and apportionment
The policyholder itemises each affected item and demonstrates, for each head of
cost claimed, the affected item to which it relates, the damage established on it,
and the making-good or recovery purpose the outlay serves.

Where an invoice line bundles indemnifiable and non-indemnifiable elements and
the elements can be identified and valued from the documents, the line is
apportioned. Where they cannot be separated, the line is assessed by its
predominant stated purpose; where the predominant purpose is not indemnifiable,
the line is not indemnified. Where a line bundles elements of a class carrying a
sub-limit, or bundles repair and recovery elements of such a class, the sub-limit
under 4.2.2 is applied to the line as a whole and, where the aggregate exceeds the
ceiling, rateably across the lines concerned.

A line is characterised by the occasion and purpose stated for it, not by the name
of the part or the operation it describes. Where a line states that the work was
carried out as part of a service, on a general check, at the policyholder's
election, or on an item found undamaged, it is not indemnifiable, and it does not
become indemnifiable by naming the same part or operation as an indemnifiable line
elsewhere in the same claim.

Labour hours, sundry materials, assembly charges, carriage and attendance charges
are allocated to the work they served; where that work is not indemnifiable, they
are not indemnifiable, and where the invoice on which they appear is directed
predominantly at work outside the cover, none of them is indemnified.

7.2 Devalued property

Insofar as property can no longer be used for its purpose, it is indemnified at
the achievable sale price.

7.3 Sum insured lower or higher than the insurable value

Where the sum insured is lower than the insurable value at the time of the insured
event, the indemnity is reduced in the proportion the sum insured bears to the
insurable value, insofar as this is agreed. Where the sum insured is higher, the
insurer is not obliged to compensate more than the loss actually incurred.

7.4 Costs

Insured costs under Part 5 are reimbursed where it is demonstrated that they were
actually incurred, and the indemnity limits agreed for each head are applied.

7.5 Order of application

The indemnity is determined in the following order: the indemnifiable loss is
established line by line under 7.1, with 7.1.9 applied to each; the lines are
allocated to their classes; the recovery costs under 5.2.2 are added within their
own limit; the class sub-limits under Part 4 are then applied, rateably where they
bite; and the deductible under 7.8 is deducted once from the resulting amount.

7.6 Replacement element of the indemnity

Where the basis of cover is the replacement value, the policyholder acquires a
claim to that part of the indemnity which exceeds the current value only where it
demonstrates that it has secured the replacement within the period under 7.1.2.

7.7 Value added tax

Value added tax is reimbursed only if and to the extent that it was actually
incurred on the occasion of the replacement or repair, and not where the
policyholder is entitled to recover input tax.

7.8 Deductible

Deductibles are deducted from the indemnity in the amount agreed, once per insured
event.

7.9 When the indemnity falls due

The indemnity falls due once the insurer has conclusively determined the claim as
to its basis and its amount. One month after notifying the loss, the policyholder
may claim as an interim payment the amount that is, on the prevailing assessment,
payable as a minimum.

7.10 Repayment

The policyholder must repay indemnity paid on the replacement basis where, through
its own fault, the property was not replaced within a reasonable period, and must
repay indemnity for property subsequently recovered and retained (2.3.2).

7.11 Interest

The indemnity bears interest from the notification of the loss, save where paid
within one month. The rate is [number] percentage point(s) below the applicable
statutory base rate, but at least [percentage] and at most [percentage] per year.

7.12 Suspension of time limits

Any period during which the indemnity cannot be determined or paid owing to the
fault of the policyholder is left out of account.

7.13 Deferral of payment

The insurer may defer payment for as long as there is doubt as to the
policyholder's entitlement to receive payment, or official or criminal proceedings
arising out of this insured event are pending.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 8 - EXPERT DETERMINATION PROCEDURE
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 After an insured event has occurred, the policyholder may require that the
amount of the loss be determined in an expert determination procedure. Insurer and
policyholder may also agree on such a procedure jointly, and may agree to extend
it to further determinations relating to the insured event.

8.2 Each party nominates one expert in text form. Where a party fails to nominate
within two weeks of a request, the requesting party may have the expert appointed
by the court with local jurisdiction for the loss location. Before beginning their
determinations, the two experts nominate a third expert as umpire.

8.3 The experts' findings must state a schedule of the taken, destroyed and
damaged insured property with the corresponding insurable values; the repair and
replacement costs; the residual values; and the insured costs. Where a class of
property carries a sub-limit, the findings state the loss for that class
separately, including the recovery costs attributable to it, so that the sub-limit
can be applied. Where an item's affected status or the making-good character of a
measure is disputed, the findings state on what evidence the answer rests.

8.4 Each expert transmits its findings to both parties simultaneously. Where the
findings diverge, the umpire decides the points that remain in dispute within the
limits set by the experts' findings. The findings are binding unless they
manifestly deviate substantially from the true state of affairs.

8.5 Unless something else has been agreed, each party bears the costs of its own
expert; the costs of the umpire are borne in equal shares.

8.6 The expert determination procedure does not affect the policyholder's duties.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 9 - POLICYHOLDER DUTIES AND INCREASE IN RISK
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 Duties before an insured event

9.1.1 The insured premises must be kept secured in the customary manner; doors and
windows must be locked when the premises are left unattended.

9.1.2 Insured property must be kept in proper condition and serviced in accordance
with the manufacturer's instructions. The cost of doing so is borne by the
policyholder (3.1.6).

9.1.3 Insured mobility equipment must, when not in immediate personal use, be
secured to a fixed object or kept in a locked room or receptacle, by means of the
locking device agreed in the schedule.

9.2 Duties after an insured event

9.2.1 The policyholder must avert and mitigate the loss so far as can reasonably
be expected and follow the insurer's instructions where these can be obtained.

9.2.2 The policyholder must report a theft or break-in without delay to the
competent public authority, notify the insurer without delay, and notify without
delay the recovery of an item that was taken (2.3.2).

9.2.3 The policyholder must provide the itemisation and evidence under 7.1.10.

9.3 Consequences of a breach of duty

Where the policyholder breaches one of these duties, and subject to the conditions
set out in the general contract provisions, the insurer is entitled to terminate
the contract and may be wholly or partly released from liability.

9.4 Increase in risk

An increase in risk subject to notification may exist in particular where the
insured premises are left unoccupied for a prolonged period, where the agreed
security or locking arrangements are altered or cease to be operational, or where
the composition or value of a class of property under 4.2 changes materially. The
consequences are governed by the general contract provisions.


-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
PART 10 - CANCELLATION AND CHANGE OF CIRCUMSTANCES
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Cancellation after an insured event

After an insured event for which the insurer has rendered a benefit, or has
declined to do so, each party may cancel the contract, observing a notice period
of one month, within one month of the conclusion of the negotiations on the
indemnity.

10.2 Change of the insured premises

Where the policyholder moves the household to other premises, cover passes to
those premises. Both sets of premises are covered during the removal, for a
maximum of [number] months. The change must be notified without delay in text
form.

10.3 Change of the rating features

Where a rating feature changes, 6.7 applies. The insurer may cancel the contract
where the policyholder does not agree to a premium adjusted in accordance with
6.7, observing a notice period of one month.

10.4 Duties of notification

Changes of the kind described in 10.2 and 10.3 must be notified without delay in
text form. Where notification has been omitted, the insurer is not obliged to pay
in the insured event only where the event occurred later than one month after
notification ought to have been received and the insurer demonstrates that it
would not have concluded the existing contract on the changed circumstances.

case.description:
A bicycle was stolen from outside the building. It was tracked down using a hidden AirTag and the police located it, but the lock had seized and a locksmith had to be called out to cut it off so the bike could be recovered.

The recovery and the repair of the theft damage were handled together by one bicycle service and billed on a single invoice covering the recovery, the locksmith work and the repair itself.
